boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Pratt Institute-Main
boards.description: Ten nearby restaurant destinations with currently published evening availability, suitable for an under-21 meal or takeout plan after campus work.

cards.title: Emily
cards.subtitle: 919 Fulton Street, Clinton Hill
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s takeout or delivery option when studio work runs long; the official location page publishes extended delivery on select nights.
cards.short_summary: A Fulton Street pizza stop with published late delivery windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Emily’s official Clinton Hill page lists delivery until 9:30 PM Thursdays and 10 PM Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists extended delivery until 9:30 PM Thursday and 10 PM Friday–Saturday; confirm ordering availability before leaving.

cards.title: Aita
cards.subtitle: 132 Greene Avenue, Clinton Hill
cards.notes: Plan a seated dinner or order ahead on Friday or Saturday; the restaurant posts an 11 PM kitchen close for those two nights.
cards.short_summary: A Greene Avenue dinner destination with late weekend kitchen hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Aita’s official site lists Friday and Saturday dinner kitchen hours from 5 PM to 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists kitchen service until 11 PM Friday and Saturday; verify reservations or takeout directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Smør Clinton Hill
cards.subtitle: 26 Putnam Avenue, Clinton Hill
cards.notes: Check the dinner schedule before heading out; its official location page lists service through 10 PM daily and 11 PM Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Putnam Avenue restaurant with dinner hours that extend into late evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Smør Clinton Hill’s official page lists dinner from 5 PM to 10 PM daily, with Friday and Saturday dinner until 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dinner until 10 PM daily and 11 PM Friday–Saturday; check the restaurant directly for changes.

cards.title: Bati Ethiopian Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 1057 Fulton Street, Clinton Hill
cards.notes: Make this an evening meal plan and check the posted dinner window; the official site lists service until 10 PM from Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A Fulton Street Ethiopian restaurant with a published 10 PM dinner close.
cards.evidence_claim: Bati Ethiopian Kitchen’s official location page lists dinner until 10 PM Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dinner until 10 PM Tuesday–Sunday; the restaurant is closed Monday according to that page.

cards.title: Colonia Verde
cards.subtitle: 219 DeKalb Avenue, Fort Greene
cards.notes: Use the weekend dinner window for a later meal near Fort Greene; the restaurant posts 11 PM closing on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A DeKalb Avenue dinner destination with late weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Colonia Verde’s official contact page lists dinner until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dinner until 11 PM Friday–Saturday and until 10 PM Sunday–Thursday; check for date-specific changes.

cards.title: Dino
cards.subtitle: 222 DeKalb Avenue, Fort Greene
cards.notes: Save this for a late Thursday-through-Saturday dinner; Dino’s official site posts an 11 PM close on each of those nights.
cards.short_summary: A DeKalb Avenue Northern Italian restaurant with 11 PM late-week hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Dino’s official site lists closing at 11 PM Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 11 PM closing Thursday–Saturday; Monday–Wednesday and Sunday are listed until 10 PM.

cards.title: Black Forest Brooklyn — Fort Greene
cards.subtitle: 733 Fulton Street, Fort Greene
cards.notes: For a later Friday or Saturday meal, use the Fort Greene location’s published midnight close and confirm the kitchen’s current service timing directly.
cards.short_summary: A Fulton Street restaurant whose official location hours extend to midnight on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Forest Brooklyn’s official site lists its Fort Greene location open until 12 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Black Forest Brooklyn — About and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Fort Greene hours until 12 AM Friday–Saturday; confirm food-service timing separately before a late visit.

cards.title: Mito — Fort Greene
cards.subtitle: 280 Ashland Place, Fort Greene
cards.notes: Use the late-week dinner window if you are already near the cultural district; the restaurant’s official site lists 11 PM closing Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: An Ashland Place Japanese restaurant with an official 11 PM weekend close.
cards.evidence_claim: Mito’s official site lists its Fort Greene location open until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours until 11 PM and other listed days until 10 PM; confirm seating or takeout availability directly.

cards.title: La Caye
cards.subtitle: 35 Lafayette Avenue, Fort Greene
cards.notes: Keep this for a Thursday-through-Saturday dinner plan; La Caye’s official page lists the restaurant open until midnight on those nights.
cards.short_summary: A Lafayette Avenue Haitian restaurant with a published midnight late-week close.
cards.evidence_claim: La Caye’s official site lists Thursday through Saturday opening hours from 4:30 PM to 12 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant hours until 12 AM Thursday–Saturday; check directly for holiday or private-event changes.

cards.title: Hops Hill
cards.subtitle: 886 Fulton Street, Clinton Hill
cards.notes: Use this Fulton Street food destination only if its current food service is confirmed before you go; its official page posts late overall venue hours.
cards.short_summary: A Clinton Hill food venue with official late-night operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Hops Hill’s official site lists its Clinton Hill location open until 4 AM Monday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, and until 2 AM on other listed days.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists late venue hours, but does not separately state kitchen hours; call ahead to confirm current food availability.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Brooklyn-campus places for research, making, viewing student work, reflection, and informal time between classes.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Brooklyn Campus Library
cards.subtitle: 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Set up at a table for research, then use the collection, scanners, printing, research help, or equipment-loan services for a project.
cards.short_summary: A landmark campus library supporting research and studio work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies its Brooklyn Campus Library as a resource-rich environment for creative teaching and learning, with collections, research support, scanning, printing, and equipment loan.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current visitor guide, hours, and borrowing policies before arriving.

cards.title: Pratt Student Union
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Use the available tables and work spaces for a study session or to meet classmates before moving on to another campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus work-space option outside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that the Brooklyn campus Student Union has tables and work spaces available for studying.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions by Parents — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Confirm building access and any event-related room changes with Pratt before visiting.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Across the 25-acre Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Take a slow loop through the lawns and use the Sculpture Park Guide to identify works; the exhibition changes over time.
cards.short_summary: An evolving outdoor collection of more than 70 sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says its Sculpture Park extends across the Brooklyn campus and includes more than 70 sculptures, with works on loan, commissioned, and periodically changing.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing conditions and individual works can change; consult Pratt’s current Sculpture Park Guide.

cards.entity_name: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery
cards.title: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery
cards.subtitle: Chemistry Building, first floor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then spend time with work by Pratt students, faculty, and alumni rather than rushing through the room.
cards.short_summary: A Chemistry Building gallery for cross-disciplinary contemporary exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the Schafler Gallery presents exhibitions by faculty, students, and alumni across departments and serves as a forum for contemporary culture.
cards.source_title: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Pratt lists gallery hours, but exhibitions and access may change; verify the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Steuben Gallery
cards.subtitle: Steuben Hall, Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition before heading over; this is a focused stop for viewing work by Pratt’s art community.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery that supports student, faculty, and alumni exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that Steuben Gallery supports exhibitions by students, faculty, and alumni during the year, including BFA thesis exhibitions.
cards.source_title: The Steuben Gallery — Pratt Institute School of Art
cards.access_notes: Exhibition schedules vary by semester; check Pratt’s current events calendar before visiting.

cards.title: ARC Building Photography Gallery
cards.subtitle: ARC Building lower level, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Time a visit around a listed photography show and use the lower-level gallery as a close look at graduating students’ displayed work.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level ARC gallery used for photography thesis exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s event page identifies the Photography Gallery in the ARC lower level and describes it as a venue for Photography BFA thesis shows within Pratt Shows.
cards.source_title: Pratt Shows: Photography BFA Thesis, Show 8 — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: The cited show has ended; consult Pratt’s current events calendar for the next exhibition and access details.

cards.title: Alumni Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn Campus Library, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Watch for a listed talk, reading, or town hall and arrive with a question; the room is used as a library event space.
cards.short_summary: A library room used for campus talks, readings, and other events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s Libraries history identifies the former Library Museum room as today’s Alumni Reading Room, used as an event space; Pratt also lists current events there.
cards.source_title: The Library Museum — Pratt Institute Libraries Special Collections
cards.access_notes: This is an event space, not a guaranteed drop-in study room; check Pratt’s events calendar and library guidance.

cards.title: Interfaith Commons
cards.subtitle: East Hall Annex, under the Pratt Chapel sign
cards.notes: Use this nondenominational room for quiet reflection or prayer, and bring or borrow the appropriate materials for your practice.
cards.short_summary: A daily-open, nondenominational reflection space in East Hall Annex.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the Interfaith Commons is a nondenominational space in the East Hall Annex, open daily for quiet reflection and prayer, with inclusive amenities and resources.
cards.access_notes: Pratt describes the space as open daily; confirm any program-related changes with Campus Ministry before visiting.

cards.title: Materials Lab
cards.subtitle: Pratt Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Use the materials resources to compare objects and surfaces while developing a project; follow any lab-specific guidance before handling collections.
cards.short_summary: A Pratt lab for hands-on material exploration and research.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt lists the Materials Lab among spaces where students can interact with collections of objects and materials and research ways of making.
cards.access_notes: Lab access, orientations, and handling rules may be program-specific; verify current requirements with Pratt.

cards.title: Cannon Plaza
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus green space
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate this named outdoor plaza, then make it a legible meeting point while moving between nearby campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor plaza shown on Pratt’s current Brooklyn campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s current Brooklyn campus map identifies Cannon Plaza among the campus’s green and open spaces.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus location; use Pratt’s current map and follow posted campus-access guidance.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named Pratt Brooklyn environments for reading, project work, computing, and production-based study, with current access details from Institute sources.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Brooklyn Library
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus library
cards.notes: Set up with your research materials in the landmarked library; use the collections, archives, and available study spaces for focused reading or project research.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with print collections, archives, and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies its Brooklyn Campus Library as a Clinton Hill landmark building with more than 200,000 print volumes, rare books, college archives, and resources supporting learning.
cards.access_notes: Pratt says the libraries support the Pratt community; visiting researchers are supported by appointment.

cards.title: Pratt Student Union
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Use the main space for independent work or meet a project team in a conference room; check with Student Union staff for room availability before planning a group session.
cards.short_summary: A student-life hub with a main space and three video-equipped conference rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt describes the Brooklyn Student Union as a place for its community to study and collaborate, with stadium seating, projector capability, and three conference rooms with video displays.
cards.access_notes: For the Pratt community; the Student Union page lists staff contact information for facility questions.

cards.title: William “Bill” Menking Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Higgins Hall Basement, 61 St. James Place
cards.notes: Bring quiet reading or architecture research to the sofas and on-site collection; sign in with the student worker and keep books in the room.
cards.short_summary: A quiet School of Architecture reading room with sofas and a non-circulating collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the School of Architecture Reading Room serves students, faculty, and staff as a place to read and study; sofas are available, and materials may not be removed.
cards.source_title: The William “Bill” Menking Book Collection | Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Service hours are Monday–Thursday, 9:30 AM–4 PM. Sign in with the student worker during service hours; no eating, drinking, or video meetings.

cards.title: Engineering Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building, second floor
cards.notes: Choose a Mac or PC workstation for software-based work; Engineering 205 adds Cintiq displays, with scanning and printing next door at the 2D Printing Center.
cards.short_summary: Four Mac and three PC classrooms with 18 workstations each.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that the Engineering Computer Lab contains four Mac and three PC classrooms with 18 workstations each, software suites, and Cintiq displays in Engineering 205.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Sunday noon–8 PM; Monday–Thursday 9 AM–9 PM; Friday 9 AM–5 PM; closed Saturday. Winter and summer schedules may change.

cards.title: Machinery Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Machinery Building, first floor
cards.notes: Use Room 101 for open Mac-platform work when you need a non-classroom setting; bring files ready for scanning or printer output.
cards.short_summary: A lab with Mac and PC classrooms, plus an always-available open Mac room.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the Machinery Computer Lab has two Mac and two PC classrooms, and that Room 101 is an open Mac-platform lab that does not hold classes and is always available to students.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Thursday 9 AM–9 PM and Friday 9 AM–5 PM; closed Saturday and Sunday. Winter and summer schedules may change.

cards.title: Foundation Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Main Building rooms 303–305; East Building room 314
cards.notes: For Foundation coursework, use iMac workstations and media tools; after 5 PM, drop in for available workstations, scanners, animation stands, or greenscreen space.
cards.short_summary: A Foundation-focused suite of iMac labs and media-production equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies the Foundation Computer Lab as a suite of iMac labs with green-screen walls and media equipment; designated workstations and equipment are available on a drop-in basis after 5 PM when classes are not in session.
cards.access_notes: Open to Foundation students, with priority for students enrolled in Time and Movement. Posted hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM–8:30 PM; closed weekends.

cards.title: Higgins Hall Labs
cards.subtitle: Higgins Hall North, second and third floors
cards.notes: Work through CAD or 3-D modeling at a PC station, then use the lab’s scanners or digital-output tools when your project needs a physical review copy.
cards.short_summary: Two computer-lab classrooms with advanced software, displays, scanners, and print tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says Higgins Hall Computer Labs have two classrooms with PCs, 27-inch HD monitors, projectors, and advanced software for CAD and 3-D models and designs.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Sunday noon–8 PM; Monday–Thursday 9 AM–9 PM; Friday 9 AM–5 PM; closed Saturday. Winter and summer schedules may change.

cards.title: 2D Printing Center
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building, second floor
cards.notes: Bring a prepared file for color, photo, or large-format output, and use staff file-preparation instruction when a project needs a production-focused work session.
cards.short_summary: A centralized campus output space for color, photo, and large-format printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies the 2D Printing Center as its centralized output area for color laser, professional photo, and large-format printing, with on-the-spot file-preparation instruction.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are 8:30 AM–midnight daily; winter and summer schedules may change. Printing uses Pratt Card funds, though each semester includes a stated free print allotment.

cards.title: 3D Printing Center
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building, second floor, Room 211
cards.notes: Use this production-focused stop to prepare a prototype or scanning plan; confirm material, submission, and appointment requirements before arriving with a file or object.
cards.short_summary: A cross-disciplinary 3-D printing and scanning hub with multiple printer types.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt describes the 3D Printing Center as its centralized hub for 3-D printing and scanning, open to students and staff of all disciplines, with printers for prototyping and presentation-quality work.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours vary by day; scans require manager approval and are by appointment only. Print submissions are made through OnePratt and charges are approved by email.

cards.title: Assembly Loop Lab
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building, Room 002, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a hands-on production session around your project file, then submit the job through OnePratt; allow added lead time during midterms and finals.
cards.short_summary: A production-services lab supporting 2-D and 3-D fabrication workflows.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt lists the Assembly Loop Lab in Engineering Building Room 002 and says its Production Services include 2-D printing, 3-D printing and scanning, digital cutting, pressure forming, and material support.
cards.access_notes: Regular posted hours: Sunday 9 AM–5 PM; Monday–Friday 9 AM–9 PM; Saturday 9 AM–5 PM. Jobs are submitted through OnePratt.

cards.notes: Use the 562 Myrtle address for a named retail browse at the campus-side end of the corridor; the neighborhood guide classifies it as a discount store.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed discount-store destination near Myrtle’s Classon end.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025 Myrtle Avenue Neighborhood Guide lists Steuben Closet at 562 Myrtle Avenue under Discount Stores.
cards.source_title: It’s on Myrtle! 2025 Myrtle Avenue Neighborhood Guide
cards.access_notes: Retail storefront; confirm current hours directly before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented, under-21-safe Pratt rituals and recurring community events, from a dawn bridge crossing to steamroller printmaking.

cards.title: Start the Year on the Brooklyn Bridge
cards.subtitle: First-year Pratt tradition
cards.notes: Join the early-morning walk only through the Institute’s announced program; it is a first-year bonding ritual led with campus leadership.
cards.short_summary: A sunrise bridge crossing marks the start of the Pratt year.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt describes an annual tradition in which first-year students join the president and vice president for student affairs for a sunrise walk across the Brooklyn Bridge.
cards.access_notes: Participate only when the Institute announces and organizes the walk.

cards.title: Cheer the Alumni Basketball Game
cards.subtitle: Cannoneer athletics tradition
cards.notes: Check Pratt Athletics and Alumni Engagement announcements for the next matchup, then attend as a spectator or reconnecting Cannoneer.
cards.short_summary: Alumni return for a recurring Cannoneer court reunion.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt documents an annual Alumni Basketball Game with records going back to 1974, organized by Pratt Athletics and Alumni Engagement.
cards.access_notes: Look for event details from Pratt Athletics or Alumni Engagement.

cards.title: Watch a Steamroller Make Prints
cards.subtitle: Annual Pratt printmaking day
cards.notes: See the public-scale printmaking process when it returns to campus; participants prepare oversized woodblocks for a visiting steamroller.
cards.short_summary: Oversized woodblocks meet a steamroller in a Pratt printmaking ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says Big Damn Prints has been an annual, daylong celebration of large-scale printmaking since arriving at Pratt in 2006.
cards.source_title: All Inky Hands on Deck - Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Follow Fine Arts or Institute announcements for the yearly event and participation details.

cards.title: Spot an Anemone in a Jar
cards.subtitle: Pratt Reef Club tradition
cards.notes: Learn about the tradition through Pratt Reef programming; Reef Club members have shared anemone from the reef in mason jars as dorm decor.
cards.short_summary: Reef Club’s unusual dorm-decor handoff comes from the campus aquarium.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies Anemone in a Jar as a Pratt tradition started under Reef Club founder TJ Holland, in which members give away anemone from the Reef in mason jars.
cards.source_title: An Unlikely On-Campus Oasis - Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Do not remove aquarium life; inquire with Reef Club about any current, supervised activity.

cards.title: Make a Costume for the Contest
cards.subtitle: October campus celebration
cards.notes: Watch Student Affairs listings each October for the annual contest and related crafting or screening programs across Pratt’s campuses.
cards.short_summary: Pratt turns Halloween into a campus-made costume celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt documents an annual Halloween costume contest as part of October celebrations across its Brooklyn and Manhattan campuses.
cards.access_notes: Check current Pratt event listings for format, entry rules, and location.

cards.title: Draw Horses on Campus
cards.subtitle: Annual School of Art and Equestrian event
cards.notes: Bring a sketchbook when the announced drawing day returns; follow staff directions and give the visiting horses plenty of space.
cards.short_summary: Pratt brings equine models onto the Brooklyn campus for a drawing day.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt calls Horses on Campus a much-anticipated annual collaboration between the School of Art and Pratt Equestrian.
cards.access_notes: Attend only during the scheduled event and follow organizers’ animal-safety guidance.

cards.title: See “The Show”
cards.subtitle: Pratt’s annual fashion runway presentation
cards.notes: Follow Pratt Shows for the yearly graduating-senior runway presentation, historically called “The Show,” and confirm current entry information.
cards.short_summary: Graduating fashion students present their collections in a long-running runway event.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that its annual fashion runway show was first presented in 1899 and describes the 2026 edition as its 125th annual runway show.
cards.source_title: Show-Stopping Looks: Pratt Fashion from Runway to Exhibition - Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current year’s venue, registration, and ticket details through Pratt Shows.

cards.title: Browse InfoShow
cards.subtitle: School of Information’s annual showcase
cards.notes: Register if required, bring photo ID, and explore student presentations, posters, object exhibitions, and interactive demonstrations.
cards.short_summary: The iSchool’s conference-style showcase gathers student work in one evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt describes InfoShow as the annual showcase and celebration of School of Information student work, organized like a conference.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event was open to the public; non-Pratt guests were asked to register and show ID at security.

cards.title: Explore the Research Open House
cards.subtitle: Annual spring research gathering
cards.notes: Look for the spring announcement, then use the open house to encounter projects from across Pratt disciplines in one shared setting.
cards.short_summary: A spring event makes Pratt research visible beyond individual studios.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt describes Research Open House as an annual spring event highlighting the range of research happening at the Institute.
cards.access_notes: Check current event details for location and attendance instructions.

cards.title: Visit the Student Design Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Pratt student maker event
cards.notes: Plan a pass through the marketplace to view student-made work and ask creators about their process; verify the next date through Pratt events.
cards.short_summary: Student makers gather to present artwork and handmade goods.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s traditions feature identifies the Student Design Marketplace and documents students selling artwork and handmade goods there in March 2024.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current event date and whether purchases are optional before visiting.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pratt Institute-Main, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that starts on Pratt’s Brooklyn campus and expands to nearby public culture and study space.

cards.title: Start at the Main Gate
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • Pratt’s Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Use the official campus map to orient yourself, identify entrances and accessible routes, then choose one campus landmark to revisit later.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a map-based campus lap.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s current Brooklyn Campus Map lists the Main Gate and identifies entrances, accessible routes, campus safety booths, and other campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Use the current online map for route and entrance details; some campus entrances are marked as requiring ID.

cards.title: Take a Slow Sculpture-Park Loop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Follow the sculpture guide at an unhurried pace and pick one work to sketch, photograph, or discuss with a new classmate.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor art walk across campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says its Sculpture Park spans the 25-acre Brooklyn campus and includes more than 70 sculptures, with works that rotate over time.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are distributed across campus; consult Pratt’s Sculpture Park guide and campus map before setting out.

cards.title: Make the Student Union Your Meet-Up Point
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Meet a hallmate or orientation contact here, compare weekend plans, and look for a low-key student program or group meeting.
cards.short_summary: A campus base for gathering and planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies the Student Union as the center of student life on the Brooklyn Campus, with areas to gather, study, relax, and collaborate.
cards.access_notes: Pratt describes it as a space for its community; confirm building access and any current program details with Student Involvement.

cards.title: Find Your Library Bearings
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Locate study areas, the archives, and equipment information before classes accelerate; save the library’s service details for your first project.
cards.short_summary: A practical campus-resource stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s self-guided tour says the Library has study spaces, rotating art exhibitions, archives, and collections including books, zines, and artist’s books.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service availability can vary; check Pratt Libraries directly before relying on a specific room or checkout service.

cards.title: Check What’s Showing at DeKalb Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday • DeKalb Hall
cards.notes: Look at the current exhibition listing before going, then spend time with one installation and read its wall text rather than rushing through.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery stop centered on student work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that DeKalb Gallery supports exhibitions by students, faculty, and alumni during the year and hosts BFA thesis exhibitions in spring.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition schedules change; verify the current show and visitor hours before traveling to the gallery.

cards.title: Compare Another Campus Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Steuben Hall
cards.notes: Pair this with DeKalb Gallery to see how two campus exhibition spaces frame different work; check the current Pratt Shows listing first.
cards.short_summary: A second on-campus art-viewing stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s Fine Arts facilities page says Steuben and DeKalb Galleries host Fine Arts Thesis exhibitions and special projects and provide curatorial opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current exhibition and hours through Pratt Shows or the gallery before visiting.

cards.title: Add the ARC Photography Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon • ARC Building
cards.notes: Check whether a photography exhibition is installed, then use the visit to notice presentation choices you might borrow for your own work.
cards.short_summary: A focused look at photography on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s 2026 campus map lists the Photography Gallery in the ARC Building Lower Level, and Pratt Shows has published BFA Photography thesis exhibitions there.
cards.access_notes: Current exhibitions are not guaranteed; verify the listing, dates, and building access before your visit.

cards.title: Set Up a Neighborhood Library Option
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning • 380 Washington Avenue
cards.notes: Make a short visit to learn the branch layout and services, then bookmark its hours for a future off-campus study or printing stop.
cards.short_summary: A nearby public-library resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Brooklyn Public Library lists Clinton Hill Library at 380 Washington Avenue with meeting rooms, after-hours returns, and printing pickup.
cards.source_title: Clinton Hill Library | Brooklyn Public Library
cards.access_notes: The branch page lists Monday–Saturday hours and Sunday closure; check it again before leaving because schedules may change.

cards.title: Take a Sunday Park Break
cards.subtitle: Sunday midday • Fort Greene
cards.notes: Use a daylight walk to reset after orientation, sit with a notebook, and identify a comfortable route back to campus before heading home.
cards.short_summary: A calm outdoor pause between campus stops.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks identifies Fort Greene Park as Brooklyn’s first park and describes its landscaped grounds and the Prison Ship Martyrs’ Monument.
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight and check NYC Parks for any weather-related closures, events, or maintenance notices.

cards.title: End With a Museum Conversation
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • 200 Eastern Parkway
cards.notes: Reserve or confirm entry, choose a single gallery or exhibition, and leave time afterward to talk through one work that stayed with you.
cards.short_summary: A museum visit that invites reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Brooklyn Museum says it is open Wednesday–Sunday, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; general-admission prices are suggested contributions, while ticketed exhibitions require a separate ticket.
cards.access_notes: Verify the date-specific hours and ticket requirements before going; ticketed exhibitions require separate admission.
